Discrepancy

diss-KREP-un-see -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, KREP. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Discrepancy is a lack of similarity between facts.

There was a small discrepancy between the ticket count and the number of people in the theater.

Worked Example

The coach's stopwatch says 12.4 seconds. The electronic timer says 12.9. Same runner, same race, same finish line -- and the two numbers refuse to agree.

That gap between two records that ought to match is a discrepancy. A discrepancy is not an opinion or a quarrel between people; it is two sets of facts that fail to line up.

How Discrepancy Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

inconsistency

inconsistency: a failure of two things to agree

mismatch

mismatch: a pair that does not fit together

variance

variance: a measured difference between two figures

Antonyms

agreement

agreement: a state of matching exactly

consistency

consistency: the quality of always matching

How Strong Is It? — variance → inconsistency → discrepancy

variance vs. discrepancy

variance vs. discrepancy: Variance is the neutral, mathematical word -- a small variance between two measurements may be perfectly normal -- while a discrepancy suggests something that ought to match and does not, and therefore needs explaining.

inconsistency vs. discrepancy

inconsistency vs. discrepancy: Inconsistency describes a whole pattern of not matching, while a discrepancy is one specific gap: a witness's story shows inconsistency across three retellings, but a single wrong date is a discrepancy.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — dis-

prefix — dis-: apart, differently (Latin)

root — crep-

root — crep-: to rattle, to creak, to make a sound (Latin crepare)

suffix — -ancy

suffix — -ancy: state or quality of (Latin -antia)

Put it together

Put it together: Discrepancy comes from Latin discrepare -- dis- ('differently') plus crepare ('to rattle, to sound') -- 'to sound different.' Two accounts that ought to ring the same note clash instead, and that jarring difference is the discrepancy.

Use the root in a new word: decrepit

Use the root in a new word: decrepit: The decrepit shed leaned so far that one more winter would finish it.

Root Check

Word Choice

Discrepancy belongs to records, figures, and accounts: a discrepancy between the two reports, an unexplained discrepancy in the totals. It needs two things that were supposed to match. People who simply disagree have a dispute, not a discrepancy -- and remember that discern, despite the look-alike spelling, is an unrelated verb about perceiving clearly.
